text:
Recent work supports modeling elapsed time separately from interaction order. [SDGI (2025)](https://www.rjdk.org.cn/rc-pub/front/front-article/download/78293911/lowqualitypdf/Session%20Recommendation%20Method%20Combining%20Sequence%20Dependency%20and%20Global%20Information.pdf) uses convolutional time-aware GRUs alongside graph components for session recommendation. [MTFNR (2026)](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-4893/19/1/3) explicitly adds time-shift and spatial-shift gates to a GRU, demonstrating a concrete mechanism for conditioning recurrence on temporal context; its geographical inputs and additional modules do not directly transfer to this Amazon task. [GRUT (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1300/) further motivates timestamps and intervals as signals of preference shifts, although its generative architecture and trend-based scoring are outside the required GRU4Rec setup.

A relevant earlier precedent, [TLSRec (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760), learns a neural time gate regulating long- versus short-term preferences. Together, these results motivate—but do not establish benchmark gains for—a single causal GRU with jointly learned temporal forgetting: feed log-scaled observed inter-event gaps into reset/update gates, or attenuate the previous hidden state before each GRU update. Content-conditioned attenuation could preserve persistent interests while reducing stale intent; hard gap-triggered resets should remain an ablation because inactivity alone does not prove intent changed. Compare ordinary GRU, gap features alone, and learned attenuation under the fixed validation protocol. Use only historical timestamps, never an unknown next-event time; skip padding updates and read the final nonpadding position of left-padded histories. All temporal components should train jointly within the one category model.
